newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia hikes internal coffee price by 12 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colombia hikes internal coffee price by 12 pct.

text.p: Colombia raised its internal coffee price by 12 percent Friday to bring it closer into line with recent increases in the world market, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said.
He said the new price, effective immediately, was set at 248,125 pesos per 125-kg load.
"This decision takes into account the convenience of passing along to producers part of the increase that we've seen on international markets," Ocampo told reporters.
Ocampo spoke after participating in the first regular policy-making meeting this year of National Coffee Growers' Federation.

The federation cut internal prices by 14,000 pesos per 125-kg load on Dec. 5. The controverisal move was aimed at reducing the deficit of the National Coffee Fund, an organization jointly administered by the government and federation executives that buys Colombian coffee at a pre-agreed support price.
Ocampo said Friday's price hike would cost the Coffee Fund about 155 billion pesos this year. ((--Juan Guillermo Londoo, Bogota newsroon, 571 610 7944))
